Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>

Subject: Private Offer: initial ask and reseller split needs

Hi Soojin / Vanessa,

Thanks again for the demo last week — CloudForge leadership is keen to move forward with a private offer on AWS Marketplace to cover our production usage. Procurement asked me to capture a few things so we can scope the PO and internal approval: 

- A line-item breakdown for the private offer (SKU mapping to your reserved capacity sku / list price)
- Expected invoice routing options (Marketplace invoice vs direct invoicing for reseller pass-through)
- Proposed reseller / distributor split mechanics (we're targeting transparent pass-through where possible)
- Any evidence or template you use to justify reseller fees (we need this for our internal audit)

Can you attach a sample pricing model and a suggested pass-through flow? We want to review with our finance and legal by Friday 6/4.

I've attached our RFP summary for context (CloudForge_RFP.pdf).

Thanks,
Samira
Samira Khan
Head of Procurement | CloudForge
samira@cloudforge.com

Subject: Re: Private Offer: initial ask and reseller split needs

Hi Samira — appreciated, and congrats on the fast internal momentum.

Quick summary of what we can provide this week: 
1) SKU mapping + two price scenarios (standard private-offer list price + a committed-usage discounted band) — attached as pricing_model_v1.xlsx.
2) Invoice routing options: 
   - Marketplace-billed (default) 
   - Reseller pass-through with invoice referencing Marketplace PO (requires reseller billing details + mapping table)
3) Channel split mechanics: we can model a pass-through % or an escrowed reseller settlement. For initial planning I included 2 scenarios in the workbook (10% straightforward pass-through; 12% with reserve/escrow holdback to cover chargebacks).
4) Evidence pack: sample invoice stub and required fields we typically provide to partners for audit.

Two quick asks from our side to make the numbers accurate: 
- Can you confirm estimated monthly token/hour profile (or expected peak qps) so we can size dedicated capacity sku?
- Do you need the reseller split to show on the Marketplace invoice or as a separate settlement?

If you want, Vanessa can run the channel routing ops for the pass-through flows. I looped her and Ben in for the ops + accounting pieces.

Best,
Soojin
Soojin Lee
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.ai
Attachment: pricing_model_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet)
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samira Khan <samira@cloudforge.com>
Date: Wed, 27 May 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private Offer: initial ask and reseller split needs

Thanks Samira / Soojin — adding ops details from the channel/invoice side.

Soojin already captured the high-level scenarios. A few operational clarifications we recommend CloudForge confirm with your finance team: 

- If you want the reseller % visible on the AWS invoice, we need the reseller's Marketplace seller ID and the reseller contract reference. That path is simplest for downstream reconciliation but requires reseller onboarding on our Marketplace listing.

- Pass-through (preferred for transparency): Redwood lists at net price; reseller invoices CloudForge separately and we settle with reseller via a monthly remittance. For audits, CloudForge will want: invoice mapping table, reseller remittance ledger, and a short attestation describing the split.

- Escrowed settlement (12% example): we withhold the reseller portion for 30 days and remit after usage verification — helpful where there's chargeback risk.

I've sketched the operational flow in the attached diagram (channel_flow_diagram.png). Also included a sample invoice stub in the pricing workbook when run with your monthly profile — FYI Ben, can you pull the typical remittance cadence for reseller partners and confirm if 30-day works?

If CloudForge can share expected monthly consumption (or a forecast range), we'll lock the SKU sizing and produce a draft PO-ready pricing attachment and a DocuSign-ready SOW/PO template.

Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Partnerships | Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai
Attachment: channel_flow_diagram.png (image)

Hi Vanessa / Soojin — this is exactly what procurement needed, thanks. A couple of follow-ups before we finalize:

> > If you want the reseller % visible on the AWS invoice, we need the reseller's Marketplace seller ID and the reseller contract reference.

We can provide the reseller seller ID and the contract reference. CloudForge prefers the reseller % to appear on the Marketplace invoice for our internal allocation.

Next steps from our side: 
- I'll confirm monthly consumption band by Monday (gross estimate: 4M tokens / ~4000 node-hours).
- Please produce a PO-ready price table and a DocuSign SOW so our legal can review next week.
- Attach our PO template (attached) — we'll want the final PO to reference CloudForge internal PO number and CloudForge Procurement as the bill-to.

Ben — if you can confirm remittance cadence (monthly works) and sample ledger fields, we'll attach those to the SOW.

If you can send the DocuSign link for the SOW/PO draft once ready that would speed approvals.

Thanks,
Samira
